claims.claim: In Next 16, middleware.ts is deprecated and renamed to proxy.ts. The file sits in the project root at the same level as app/. It exports a function named `proxy` (a default export also works), plus an optional `export const config = { matcher }`. Proxy always runs on the Node.js runtime: a `runtime` segment config in proxy throws, and edge is not supported. Without a matcher it runs on every request, including _next/static and public assets.

claims.claim: Without Cache Components, a page that uses no request-time APIs is prerendered at build time. With Cache Components, a GET route handler that reads no uncached or runtime data is prerendered too. better-sqlite3 calls are synchronous, so Next probably cannot see them as I/O. A server page that reads hours or branches from SQLite, or a GET handler that reads neither the request nor the network, could then be frozen at `next build`. `await connection()` from 'next/server' (or reading the request) makes rendering wait for a real request in both modes.

claims.claim: sqlite3_busy_timeout installs a handler that sleeps repeatedly until at least the given number of ms has passed, then returns SQLITE_BUSY. claims.claim: WAL does not work over a network filesystem: every process using the database must be on the same host. WAL can still return SQLITE_BUSY briefly while the last connection closes or when recovery runs after a crash.

deviations.default: "Error mapping ... err.code === 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_TRIGGER' with message exactly TABLE_OVERLAP → SLOT_TAKEN; GUEST_OVERLAP → DUPLICATE_BOOKING. SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE with a message naming reservations.idempotency_key → look the key up again (step 1)."
deviations.finding: BEFORE INSERT triggers run before UNIQUE checks, so a same-key replay that reaches INSERT surfaces as GUEST_OVERLAP (1811), not as the UNIQUE error. It would be mapped to a 409 DUPLICATE_BOOKING instead of returning the same booking with 200 (SQ-24). When both overlap conditions hold, the order in which the two triggers fire is undocumented. GUEST_OVERLAP fired first on 3.51.0 and 3.54.1 (SQ-25). The UNIQUE path is only reachable for a different body on a non-overlapping slot. Inside a correct IMMEDIATE transaction step 1 always sees committed rows, so these paths are defence-in-depth only.
deviations.recommendation: On any err.code starting with 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT', after the transaction has rolled back, first repeat the step-1 lookup by idempotency_key: same hash → return the row with 200, different hash → IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH. Only then map TABLE_OVERLAP → SLOT_TAKEN, GUEST_OVERLAP → DUPLICATE_BOOKING, and UNIQUE(idempotency_key) → re-lookup. Keep the 'starts with SQLITE_BUSY' rule; it covers SQLITE_BUSY and SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT/RECOVERY. Do not write tests that assert which trigger message wins when both conditions hold.

deviations.default: "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;   -- per connection; also set journal_mode=WAL and busy_timeout=5000 on open" as the first line of the DDL block (which becomes migrations/*.sql)
deviations.finding: If migrate.ts runs each migration inside db.transaction(), as it should, PRAGMA foreign_keys inside it is a silent no-op. PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL inside a transaction on a non-WAL database fails with 'cannot change into wal mode from within a transaction' (SQ-35). better-sqlite3 already compiles in DEFAULT_FOREIGN_KEYS=1 and defaults timeout to 5000 (SQ-01, SQ-10), but other tools such as /usr/bin/sqlite3 do not.
deviations.recommendation: Keep all PRAGMAs out of the migration files. In lib/db/client.ts openDb(): new Database(path, { timeout: 5000 }) with an explicit timeout; then db.pragma('journal_mode = WAL'), asserting the result is 'wal'; then db.pragma('foreign_keys = ON'); optionally db.pragma('synchronous = FULL') (see the 5.6 durability entry). All of this runs before any transaction. Migration files contain DDL only, and each is applied in db.transaction(...).immediate().

deviations.default: "-- Add matching BEFORE UPDATE triggers (excluding r.id = NEW.id) so a status change back to 'confirmed' or a time/table change can't create an overlap."
deviations.finding: Excluding by NEW.id gives a false TABLE_OVERLAP or GUEST_OVERLAP whenever a confirmed row's id changes, because the row's OLD version is still in the table during BEFORE UPDATE (SQ-28). Excluding by OLD.id behaves correctly. Plain BEFORE UPDATE ... WHEN NEW.status='confirmed', with no column list, covers status, time, table, phone and branch changes; all were tested.
deviations.recommendation: Use the tested triggers in the artifact 'reservations_update_triggers.sql': BEFORE UPDATE ON reservations WHEN NEW.status = 'confirmed', excluding 'r.id <> OLD.id'.

deviations.default: "createReservation ... runs synchronously inside one better-sqlite3 IMMEDIATE transaction (db.transaction(fn).immediate(...); transaction functions must not be async)"
deviations.finding: This is correct, but two details matter. (1) If createReservation is ever called while db.inTransaction is true, .immediate() becomes a SAVEPOINT and no write lock is taken up front (SQ-04). (2) An async fn does not 'commit early' as api.md says. 13.0.3 throws TypeError('Transaction function cannot return a promise') and rolls back the synchronous prefix, while code after the first await still runs later in autocommit mode (SQ-05). The empirical DEFERRED race shows what losing IMMEDIATE costs: 19 of 20 get SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT in about 33 ms, not SLOT_TAKEN (SQ-62).
deviations.recommendation: In createReservation, assert !db.inTransaction before calling tx.immediate(). Wrap db.transaction in a typed helper whose callback type rejects Promise return types, so async functions fail type-checking. Keep the 6.1 assertion '19 SLOT_TAKEN', which already catches a regression to DEFERRED.

deviations.default: "G-3: A confirmation is shown only after commit, from the saved row." / "Limits: one database file on a local disk on one machine; not valid over network filesystems."
deviations.finding: The bundled build defaults WAL databases to synchronous=NORMAL (SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_SYNCHRONOUS=1). A commit is durable across app crashes, but might roll back after a power loss or OS crash (SQ-54). The network-filesystem limit is confirmed by wal.html (SQ-52).
deviations.recommendation: Either set db.pragma('synchronous = FULL') on open (the extra cost is inferred to be negligible at demo write volume), or add a line to the README Limits: 'with the default synchronous=NORMAL in WAL mode, a booking confirmed just before a power loss or OS crash could be lost'. I recommend FULL, so the guarantee can be stated without that caveat.

deviations.default: service_hours/hours_exceptions: "opens TEXT NOT NULL, closes TEXT NOT NULL, CHECK (closes > opens)"; "date TEXT NOT NULL"; "is_closed INTEGER NOT NULL"
deviations.finding: Comparing text only works for zero-padded 'HH:MM'. Unpadded '9:00'-'12:00' is wrongly rejected; '12:00'-'9:30' and 'abc'-'abd' are wrongly accepted. The date column accepts 'tomorrow', and is_closed has no domain check (SQ-31).
deviations.recommendation: Add the tested CHECKs: opens/closes GLOB '[0-2][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]' with opens < '24:00' and closes <= '24:00'; date GLOB '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]-[0-9][0-9]' AND date(date) IS date; is_closed IN (0,1). Keep Zod validation in the seed loader as the first line of defence.

deviations.default: reservations: "branch_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES branches(id), table_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dining_tables(id)"
deviations.finding: The DB accepts a reservation whose table belongs to the other branch (SQ-33). The branch-scoped guest trigger and the availability checks then disagree with the table actually used.
deviations.recommendation: Add UNIQUE (branch_id, id) to dining_tables, and FOREIGN KEY (branch_id, table_id) REFERENCES dining_tables(branch_id, id) to reservations. Tested: this rejects the mismatch with SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_FOREIGNKEY. Optionally add indexes (table_id, starts_at) and (branch_id, phone_e164, starts_at) to back the trigger lookups; at demo scale they are not needed (inferred).

deviations.default: "-- The seed loader rejects a whole-day row that coexists with per-service rows for the same date."
deviations.finding: The partial unique indexes work as intended (SQ-32), but as the comment says, only the loader prevents a whole-day row from coexisting with per-service rows. The DB accepted that combination.
deviations.recommendation: Keep the loader check and add a unit test for it. Optionally add BEFORE INSERT triggers on hours_exceptions that RAISE(ABORT,'EXCEPTION_CONFLICT') when the opposite kind of row exists for the same (branch_id, date).

deviations.default: "SQLite via better-sqlite3, WAL mode, foreign keys on, busy timeout 5000 ms"
deviations.finding: Confirmed and compatible. better-sqlite3 13.0.3 defaults timeout to 5000 and FKs to on, ships an N-API (v10) darwin-arm64 prebuild inside the tarball with no install script, and Next 16.4.2 externalises it by default (SQ-01, SQ-10, SQ-11, SQ-14). 13.0.0, a full node-addon-api rewrite, is only about 3 months old (released 2026-07-21), and none of it was run here.
deviations.recommendation: Keep 13.0.3, pinned exactly. In Phase 4, run the 5.6 error-mapping unit tests and the 6.1 race in Node first, as the gate for this choice. Fallback if the N-API build misbehaves: 12.12.0, which uses prebuild-install and bundles SQLite 3.53.3; I did not verify it supports Node 26.

deviations.default: "Lexical search: an SQLite FTS5 table." Evidence: "FTS5 is compiled into better-sqlite3's bundled SQLite [Unverified; verify in Phase 2]"
deviations.finding: FTS5 is compiled in: SQLITE_ENABLE_FTS5 appears in defines.gypi, in compilation.md and in the prebuild's strings (SQ-10). Binding raw guest text to MATCH throws on '?', "'", '-', '.', unbalanced quotes, empty input and leading NOT, and silently reinterprets ':', '*', '^', '{...}' and uppercase AND/OR/NOT/NEAR (SQ-41). Porter does not bridge 'spicy'/'spice' or 'kid'/'children' (SQ-43).
deviations.recommendation: Update the D-02 evidence to Verified. Use the tested DDL `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE kb_fts USING fts5(fact_id UNINDEXED, body, tokenize = 'porter unicode61 remove_diacritics 2')`. Build the MATCH string only with the sanitiser: extract /[\p{L}\p{N}]+/gu tokens, lower-case, cap at 16, double-quote each with embedded quotes doubled, join with ' OR ', bind as a parameter, and skip the lexical search when there are no tokens. Order by bm25(kb_fts), then fact_id. Rebuild the table inside the kb:index transaction. Add the raw-input strings from SQ-41 as unit-test cases that must not throw.

deviations.default: "Concurrency test (B): ... 20 children ... Assert one created, 19 SLOT_TAKEN, exactly 1 row, and no child exiting non-zero. Repeat 10 times; test timeout 120 s."
deviations.finding: The design is sound. A Python and SQLite equivalent passed 10 of 10 runs, with losers seeing the committed row and max waits of 0.15-0.48 s (SQ-60). Two refinements would sharpen it. A trigger-only variant (app checks skipped) proves the DB backstop: 19 TABLE_OVERLAP (SQ-61). And waits only approach the 5 s busy timeout if each transaction holds the lock for about 250 ms or more (SQ-63).
deviations.recommendation: Keep the test as specified. Also assert that no child reports SQLITE_BUSY or UNAVAILABLE, and that every SLOT_TAKEN child saw 1 row. Add a second test that inserts directly and expects 19 SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_TRIGGER 'TABLE_OVERLAP'. Do nothing slow inside the transaction (hashing and validation happen before it). Run unit tests of SQL behaviour against better-sqlite3, not /usr/bin/sqlite3, because the system CLI has DQS=3 and extra options (SQ-34).

artifacts.content:
-- BEFORE UPDATE companions to no_table_overlap_ins / no_guest_overlap_ins (MASTER_PROMPT 5.4).
-- Exclude the row being updated by OLD.id (its current version in the table), not NEW.id.
CREATE TRIGGER no_table_overlap_upd BEFORE UPDATE ON reservations WHEN NEW.status = 'confirmed'
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'TABLE_OVERLAP') WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM reservations r WHERE r.id <> OLD.id AND r.table_id = NEW.table_id AND r.status = 'confirmed'
      AND r.starts_at < NEW.ends_at AND NEW.starts_at < r.ends_at);
END;
CREATE TRIGGER no_guest_overlap_upd BEFORE UPDATE ON reservations WHEN NEW.status = 'confirmed'
BEGIN
  SELECT RAISE(ABORT, 'GUEST_OVERLAP') WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM reservations r WHERE r.id <> OLD.id AND r.branch_id = NEW.branch_id AND r.phone_e164 = NEW.phone_e164
      AND r.status = 'confirmed' AND r.starts_at < NEW.ends_at AND NEW.starts_at < r.ends_at);
END;

artifact_checks.notes: I applied the verbatim artifact text (work/artifact_update_triggers.sql) after the 5.4 DDL on 3.51.0 and 3.54.1. Re-confirming an overlapping cancelled row -> TABLE_OVERLAP. Moving a row onto an occupied table/time -> TABLE_OVERLAP. Changing phone+time into another booking of the same guest -> GUEST_OVERLAP. artifact_checks.name: kb_fts.sql
artifact_checks.notes: The exact DDL and the query 'ORDER BY bm25(kb_fts), fact_id LIMIT 8' work on 3.54.1 (Python) and 3.51.0 (/usr/bin/sqlite3 CLI and Python). The fact_id tie-break matters, because common terms give bm25 of -0.0 ties ('veg*', 'rs'). I ran the JS port in Node 26.12.0, and it gives the same strings as the Python [^\W_]+ version for the whole raw-input list; no sanitised string caused an FTS5 error (0 errors over 35+ inputs). Caveat: NFD-decomposed input ('crème brûlée'.normalize('NFD')) splits into 'cre','me','bru','le','e' and misses menu:creme-brulee (it matched faq:email instead). FTS5 unicode61's default token categories are 'L* N* Co' (fts5.html), so combining marks act as separators. Lower-casing before matching can also add combining marks ('İstanbul' -> 'i','stanbul'). Fix: text.normalize('NFKC') before tokenising, on both index and query sides. Lower-casing is optional, because unicode61 folds case.

missed: Deviation 5.1's fallback is wrong. better-sqlite3 12.12.0 does not exist: `npm view better-sqlite3 versions` ends ...12.10.1, 12.11.1, 13.0.0-13.0.3. The latest 12.x is 12.11.1, which bundles SQLite 3.53.2, not 3.53.3 (unpkg 12.11.1/deps/download.sh VERSION="3530200"). It declares engines 'node: 20.x || ... || 26.x' and install script 'prebuild-install || node-gyp rebuild --release'. The GitHub release v12.11.1 has the asset better-sqlite3-v12.11.1-node-v147-darwin-arm64.tar.gz (Node 26 = modules 147, verified with process.versions.modules), so it would download a prebuild from GitHub over the network at install time. The fallback should read 12.11.1.

FTS5 sanitiser: normalise Unicode before tokenising. The FTS5 unicode61 default categories are 'L* N* Co' (https://www.sqlite.org/fts5.html: 'The default value is "L* N* Co"'), so combining marks (Mn/Mc) are separators. NFD input such as a pasted 'crème brûlée' fragments into 'cre','me',... and fails to retrieve the NFC-indexed fact (verified in vfts.py). Apply text.normalize('NFKC') to both rendered fact lines and guest text, and lower-case after matching or not at all: 'İ'.toLowerCase() adds U+0307 and splits the token.

Async transaction function: besides the TypeError and rollback, the wrapper discards the promise. If the async continuation rejects, Node 26's default --unhandled-rejections=throw raises it as an uncaught exception unless an unhandledRejection hook is installed (nodejs.org/docs/latest-v26.x/api/cli.html). @types/better-sqlite3 9.6.0 declares transaction<F extends VariableArgFunction>(fn: F), which accepts async functions, so TypeScript will not catch this without the typed helper the researcher proposed (verified in unpkg index.d.ts lines 36-62).

db.pragma() returns an array of row objects ([{journal_mode:'wal'}]) unless called with { simple: true } (lib/methods/pragma.js: 'return simple ? stmt.pluck().get() : stmt.all()'). The 'assert result is wal' recommendation needs db.pragma('journal_mode = WAL', { simple: true }) === 'wal'. @types gives the return type as unknown.

synchronous differs between first and later runs. A connection that itself switches a fresh DB to WAL keeps the non-WAL default synchronous=2 (FULL). Later opens of the existing WAL file get SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_SYNCHRONOUS=1 (NORMAL). I verified this on the 3.51.0 build, which has DEFAULT_WAL_SYNCHRONOUS=1 like the bundled build: 'synchronous = (2,)' after switching, '(1,)' after reopening. Durability would silently change after the first restart, which is another reason to set PRAGMA synchronous explicitly on every open. pragma.html: 'A transaction committed in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL might roll back following a power loss or system crash.'

Busy waits grow faster than the serial lock time on builds without SETLK_TIMEOUT, such as the bundled one, because of sleep/backoff polling. In the trigger-only race on 3.54.1 with every child holding the lock: 20 ms hold -> max wait about 1.5 s; 60 ms -> 1.9 s; 100 ms -> 2.4 s; 250 ms -> 5.2 s, with 2 of 20 children getting SQLITE_BUSY at BEGIN IMMEDIATE. This supports the researcher's ~250 ms figure (SQ-63) and their advice to do nothing slow inside the transaction. In the server, a busy wait also blocks the whole Next.js event loop synchronously for up to 5 s, though contention only comes from other processes (seed/migrate scripts, tests, a second dev server). The event-loop point is Inferred.

Alternative to the 5.6 re-lookup rule (optional): making the overlap triggers AFTER INSERT (excluding r.id <> NEW.id) would let UNIQUE(idempotency_key) fire before the overlap check, so a same-key replay maps to the idempotency path, as 5.6 originally assumed. sqlite.org itself says 'programmers are encouraged to prefer AFTER triggers over BEFORE triggers'. Its cautions concern BEFORE triggers that modify rows, which these do not, so the current BEFORE triggers are safe and the researcher's 're-lookup on any SQLITE_CONSTRAINT*' rule is enough. The AFTER-trigger ordering itself is Inferred from SQLite's insert order and was not run.

The '3.54.1' engine used for the empirical checks (Homebrew Python 3.14.5, and Node 26's node:sqlite) is the Homebrew shared library /opt/homebrew/opt/sqlite/lib/libsqlite3.dylib (otool -L /opt/homebrew/bin/node). It has DEFAULT_WAL_SYNCHRONOUS=2 and THREADSAFE=1, unlike the bundled build, and it changes with `brew upgrade sqlite`. Node reports process.versions.sqlite '3.54.0' while sqlite_version() returns '3.54.1'. DECISIONS D-03's 'node:sqlite (SQLite 3.54.1)' is only true for the current Homebrew sqlite. No engine tested so far is the exact bundled 3.53.4 build, so the Phase 4 better-sqlite3 tests remain the real gate.

Who wins between duplicate UNIQUE constraints is also unspecified. With both id and idempotency_key duplicated, the error names reservations.idempotency_key (vddl.py A9b). Ids should be generated server-side so this cannot happen, and the error mapping should not rely on which UNIQUE message wins.

deviations.default: "Context trap: Ollama defaults to a 4k context on machines with under 24 GiB of VRAM, so always send `num_ctx`. If `prompt_eval_count ≥ num_ctx − 512`, throw `CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`. Never rely on truncation."
deviations.finding: The 4096 default is correct for this Mac (17.8 GiB Metal VRAM), but qwen3.5 runs on the MLX runner. There, chat truncation is disabled (routes.go sets truncate=false for MLX), the hard limit is the model maximum (262144), and num_ctx is a soft, load-time value that does not trigger a reload. Whoever loads the model first fixes the /api/ps context_length; it stayed 4096 when I sent 8192. The guard still works because prompt_eval_count is the full prompt on MLX.
deviations.recommendation: Keep sending num_ctx: 8192 and keep the CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE guard as an app-level prompt budget, but reword the rationale: on MLX there is no truncation, the risk is latency and memory. model:check should report /api/ps `runner` and `context_length` and warn if context_length is below the configured num_ctx (another client loaded the model first). Also send `"truncate": false` on /api/chat (a source-only field in v0.40.5) so a llama.cpp-runner model errors instead of silently dropping messages.

deviations.default: `options: { temperature: 0, seed: 42, num_ctx: 8192, num_predict: 400 }`
deviations.finding: Both qwen3.5 Modelfiles set presence_penalty 1.5. The MLX sampler applies it before argmax even at temperature 0, over a window seeded with the last repeat_last_n (64) prompt tokens, which contain the guest message. Copying guest values into booking fields is therefore biased against. Also, seed:42 has no effect at temperature 0.
deviations.recommendation: Add `presence_penalty: 0` and `repeat_last_n: 0` (which disables the penalty ring); optionally `frequency_penalty: 0`. A/B this in the Phase 2 probe on the 10 extraction cases and record the result in DECISIONS.md. Keep seed for harmlessness, but attribute repeatability to greedy decoding and check output identity across the 3 probe runs (9b uses speculative decoding, draft_num_predict 3).

deviations.default: "Prompt layout (static first, so Ollama can reuse the cached prefix)"
deviations.finding: For qwen3.5 (hybrid recurrent layers) on MLX, the cache resumes only at snapshot offsets (earlier prompt ends or branch points), not at the longest shared prefix. The same ~294-token static system prompt with a new guest message gave prompt_eval_cached_count 0 and a full 995 ms prefill. Reuse appears only after a snapshot exists at or before the divergence point.
deviations.recommendation: Keep the static block first and byte-identical (no clock, session or retrieved data), ending at a fixed delimiter, with all dynamic content (time, draft, D-02 retrieved facts, history, guest message) after it. Have `model:warm` send two requests with the full static prefix whose dynamic parts differ at the first token after the delimiter, which plants a snapshot exactly at the static boundary. The probe must measure prompt_eval_cached_count and latency over distinct messages (not repeats) and report the first post-load call separately. Tests must not assert cache hits.

deviations.default: "Measure ... `ollama ps` size and GPU share with the browser open" and selection rule "... warm p95 ≤ 4 s and 100% GPU"
deviations.finding: /api/ps has no processor field. On Apple unified memory size_vram equals size for every model (MLX and llama.cpp), so '100% GPU' is always met. The real constraint is system memory: MLX resident size grows with prefix-cache snapshots (4b went 4.25 to 8.69 GB; snapshot eviction threshold is 8 GiB), and with 9b, 4b and the embedder resident the scheduler logged only 2.7 GiB free system memory. Another local client was also using Ollama during this research, which contaminates timings.
deviations.recommendation: Compute GPU share as size_vram/size and record /api/ps size at the end of each run, not just after load. Add a system-memory criterion, e.g. free memory ≥ a set number of GiB with the browser open. Probe each chat model alone (keep_alive: 0 or unload before switching models). Before timing, confirm exclusive access: /api/ps empty and no foreign requests in ~/.ollama/logs/server.log.

deviations.default: "Record `prompt_eval_count`, `prompt_eval_cached_count`, `eval_count` and the duration fields (nanoseconds → ms)."
deviations.finding: The field exists with this exact name, but it is optional (`*int`, omitempty) and absent from /api/embed responses. prompt_eval_count includes cached tokens, and prompt_eval_duration covers only uncached tokens.
deviations.recommendation: Type it as `number | undefined` in the Zod response schema and store null when absent. Derive uncached tokens as prompt_eval_count − (prompt_eval_cached_count ?? 0).

deviations.default: "`npm run model:check`: Ollama version, model present plus digest, a schema round-trip, measured warm latency, `num_ctx` in effect."
deviations.finding: /api/tags details for qwen3.5:9b have a blank parameter_size, quantization_level and family; /api/show has them (9.7B, nvfp4). Thinking control metadata is only in /api/show (`thinking.values` / `default`). For MLX, '`num_ctx` in effect' as shown by /api/ps is soft and set by the first loader.
deviations.recommendation: model:check should read the digest from /api/tags; read details, capabilities (must include completion) and thinking.values (must include false) from /api/show; and report /api/ps runner and context_length. It should also run the schema round-trip with the real evals/fixtures/turn.schema.json and fail on HTTP 400 'invalid structured output grammar'.

deviations.default: "Semantic search: vectors from a local Ollama embedding model (`/api/embed`), stored as BLOBs in `fact_embeddings(fact_id, model, content_hash, dim, vector)`, with brute-force cosine in TypeScript."
deviations.finding: qwen3-embedding:0.6b returns 1024-dim, unit-length vectors. Its card asks for an instruction prefix on queries only. /api/embed truncates silently by default (truncate: true), and the model runs on llama.cpp at a 4096 context, with a 4.4 s cold load and 1.24 GB resident.
deviations.recommendation: Embed documents as raw fact lines. Embed queries as `Instruct: <English task description>\nQuery:<masked text>`. Send `truncate: false`. Store all 1024 dims as Float32 (4096 B) and do not pass `dimensions`. Use a dot product, since vectors are normalised. Include the embedding model name and instruction string in the cache key/content_hash, and warm the embedder in model:warm. Count its ~1.24 GB in the memory budget.

deviations.default: Call the model. Validate with Zod. On invalid output, retry once with a short corrective message.
deviations.finding: Grammar-constrained decoding nearly always returns output that passes Zod, even when content is lost. answer is cut at exactly 600 chars mid-word, citedFactIds is cut to the first 8, and integers are clamped. The retry path does not catch these. Truly invalid output mostly comes from hitting num_predict (done_reason 'length').
deviations.recommendation: Treat done_reason === 'length' as invalid (retry, then degrade). Treat answer.length === 600 as truncated (use the fixed fallback, or drop the prose). Set num_predict to bound latency. Keep the prompt rule of replies under 60 words.

Under the default min metadata, isValid() checks length only. README 1.13.15 line 658: 'effectively causing isValid() to behave same way as if it was isPossible()'. The recommended single /max module with MOBILE|FIXED_LINE_OR_MOBILE is still the right choice, because the same module also does text finding for grounding and masking.
